ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Assume that the rational function A(q)/B(q) is a polynomial in Z[q]. Then there exists a polynomial C(q) in Z[q] such that

A(q)=B(q)C(q).

Because A(q) and B(q) are both nonzero, C(q) must also be nonzero: if C(q)=0, then A(q)=B(q)C(q)=0, contradicting that A(q) is nonzero.

Now let r=deg(B) and s=deg(C). Since B and C are nonzero, we may write

B(q)=b_r q^r + b_{r-1} q^{r-1}+\cdots+b_0, with b_r\neq 0,
C(q)=c_s q^s + c_{s-1} q^{s-1}+\cdots+c_0, with c_s\neq 0.

In the product B(q)C(q), every term has degree at most r+s, because it comes from multiplying q^i by q^j with i\le r and j\le s. The coefficient of q^{r+s} is b_r c_s, which is nonzero because b_r and c_s are nonzero integers. Therefore the product B(q)C(q) has degree exactly r+s. Hence

deg(A)=deg(B(q)C(q))=r+s=deg(B)+deg(C).

Since C is a nonzero polynomial, deg(C)=s\ge 0. Therefore

deg(A)=deg(B)+deg(C)\ge deg(B).

This proves that deg(A)\ge deg(B).
payload.role_in_assembly: Converts the assumption that the reduced quotient is a polynomial into an inequality between the degrees of its numerator and denominator.

domain_restrictions: A and B must be nonzero polynomials so that their degrees are defined and the quotient is meaningful as a rational function.
A and B lie in the polynomial ring with integer coefficients in q.
The hypothesis that A divided by B is itself a polynomial means the rational function has no remaining denominator after simplification and is an element of the same polynomial ring.

quantifier_order: For all polynomials A and B with integer coefficients in q, assuming both are nonzero, if the quotient A divided by B is itself a polynomial with integer coefficients in q, then the degree of A is at least the degree of B.

payload.statement_nl: Let A(q) and B(q) be nonzero polynomials in Z[q]. If the rational function A(q) / B(q) is itself a polynomial in Z[q], then deg(A) >= deg(B).

dependency_assessment.notes: No solver-declared citations were used; the argument is self-contained and does not rely on forbidden ancestry claims.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly expands the meaning of the quotient being a polynomial as existence of C in Z[q] with A = B C.
The degree computation is valid because the leading coefficient of BC is b_r c_s, which is nonzero in Z.
The conclusion deg(A) >= deg(B) follows immediately from deg(A) = deg(B) + deg(C) and C nonzero.

result_payload.reason: The proof is mathematically correct and complete for the stated lemma. From the hypothesis that A(q)/B(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], it introduces C(q) with A = BC, uses nonzeroness of A and B to conclude C is nonzero, and then proves deg(BC) = deg(B) + deg(C) by inspecting leading terms. Since deg(C) >= 0, it follows that deg(A) >= deg(B). This matches the lemma sketch and the stated assembly role.
